title: Exec-chain safety: tokenized handshake and result curation
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: Multi-tool chains in the Exec loop are increasingly common (function calls, external tools, and synthetic transformers). We're seeing two classes of failures in production: accidental recursion (tool A calls tool B which calls A), and heuristic result injection that corrupts downstream structured outputs. This ticket scopes a protocol + runtime changes to introduce a lightweight tokenized handshake for each tool invocation, deterministic result curation rules, and loop detection/mitigation that operate under streaming responses and legacy compatibility layers.

Goals:
- Prevent recursive loops and uncontrolled repetition across tool chains without blocking legitimate retries.
- Provide a deterministic, schema-backed result curation step so downstream prompts receive sanitized, structured payloads (for structured outputs, function calls, and embeddings).
- Maintain streaming behavior (partial tool outputs) while ensuring provenance and idempotency for partial commits.
- Keep compatibility with older SDKs and console views via a compatibility shim.

Non-goals:
- Full redesign of the runtime planner or batcher. This is an incremental protocol and runtime guard set that can be toggled per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake token attached to every tool invocation and replayed in downstream calls
Loop detector prevents more than N cross-tool handoffs within a rolling window and emits telemetry/alert
Result curation enforces declared output schema and rejects or sanitizes unexpected fields with clear diagnostics
Streaming partial results can be committed as provisional entries with provenance tokens and later finalized
Backward compatibility mode exposes sanitized payloads to older SDKs while tagging which fields were removed or truncated
implementation_notes: Implement handshake as a 3-field header: request_token, parent_token, ttl_ms. Request tokens are RFC4122 v4 with a compact base62 encoding to save wire overhead.

Loop detector: maintain per-session LRU of recent request_token values and parent_token edges; trigger soft-fail after threshold T (configurable per-customer). Soft-fail means: halt further automatic tool fanout and return a structured 'loop_detected' result with details.

Result curation: apply declared output schema from tool manifest (JSON Schema subset). If schema mismatch, attempt safe coercions (stringify numbers, trim arrays) then if still invalid attach 'curation_errors' and drop unexpected keys unless 'preserve_unexpected' flag is set for tenant.

Streaming: partial outputs carry the same request_token and provisional sequence number. Runtime will persist provisional KV until final commit; provisional commits are labeled with provenance: request_token:seq. Consumers can opt into 'provisional' vs 'final' streams.
Compatibility shim: when SDK version < 1.15, we degrade to a flattened payload and include a compatibility header 'x-rw-compat: exec-chain-v1' describing removed keys and a short diagnostic URL.

Telemetry: emit a 'exec_chain_handoff' event with tags: source_tool, dest_tool, request_token, depth, curation_result (ok|coerced|dropped), and loop_signal if any. Incremental sampling at 5% plus full samples for loop events.
Security: handshake tokens must be HMAC-signed when crossing tenant boundaries (private deployments) to prevent replay attacks. Public hosted mode uses ephemeral tokens with short ttl_ms by default.
progress_comments: 2025-11-13 - Spike complete: prototype handshake header and basic loop detector in local executor. Verified base62 token fits current telemetry wire budget. (Liam)
2025-11-18 - Design review: PM and Runtime leads prefer soft-fail behavior to keep consumer apps stable. Agreed to make threshold T tenant-configurable. (Design feedback: Claudia Rivera)
2025-11-21 - Security review kickoff: draft HMAC signing approach for cross-tenant handoffs. Pending key management integration with KMS. (Security: Rajesh Kumar)
2025-11-26 - UX note: Console team wants 'provisional' markers surfaced in streaming logs. Created follow-up ticket PM-412 for console surface work. (Asha)

2025-11-30 - Implementer update: provisional commits persisted to redis with 24h TTL; adding finalize RPC to promote provisional->final. Created WIP PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987. (Asha)
2025-12-02 - QA: unit tests for coercion rules (numbers->strings, array trimming) added. Found edge-case where nested unexpected keys were not being dropped; fixed in branch. (QA: Morgan Lee)
2025-12-03 - Blocker: Redis cluster client library upgrade required to support async finalize RPC semantics. Engineering lead approved dependency bump but requires staging soak. (Liam)
2025-12-03 - Next: finalize API sketch for handshake header, land telemetry schema, and run a mixed-traffic canary for 5% of hosted traffic after staging soak. (Asha)
notes_for_reviewers: Key trade-offs: soft-fail vs hard-fail behavior for loops (we chose soft-fail), aggressive schema coercion vs conservative rejection (we chose conservative but with safe coercions). Reviewers should pay attention to compatibility shim contract and telemetry field names. KMS integration for HMAC signing is tracked separately.
